claim: Answer / body: OAuth 2.0 is the IETF framework in RFC 6749.
quote: The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework

claim: Answer / FAQ 1: it gives a third-party app limited access to an HTTP service on behalf of the user.
quote: The OAuth 2.0 authorization framework enables a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service

claim: Body: instead of using the owner's credentials, the client obtains an access token denoting scope and lifetime.
quote: Instead of using the resource owner's credentials to access protected resources, the client obtains an access token -- a string denoting a specific scope, lifetime, and other access attributes.

claim: Body / FAQ 3: refresh tokens are used to obtain a new access token when the current one expires.
quote: Refresh tokens are credentials used to obtain access tokens.

claim: Body: scope strings are defined by each authorization server.
quote: The strings are defined by the authorization server.

claim: Body: RFC 6749 recommends the state parameter and says it should be used to prevent CSRF.
quote: The parameter SHOULD be used for preventing cross-site request forgery as described in Section 10.12.

claim: Body: PKCE (RFC 7636) mitigates authorization code interception.
quote: OAuth 2.0 public clients utilizing the Authorization Code Grant are susceptible to the authorization code interception attack.

claim: Body: PKCE stands for Proof Key for Code Exchange.
quote: Proof Key for Code Exchange

claim: Answer / body: Strava documents the authorization-code flow.
quote: If the user authorized the application, the URL query string will include an authorization code and the scope accepted by the user.

claim: Answer / body: the code is exchanged for a refresh token and a short-lived access token.
quote: Applications complete the authorization process by exchanging the authorization code for a refresh token and short-lived access token.

claim: Body: Strava lets the user opt out of requested scopes.
quote: A user can opt out of the scopes requested by the application.

claim: Answer / body: users can grant and revoke access per application.
quote: It allows users to grant and revoke API access on a per-application basis and keeps users' authentication details safe.

claim: Table / FAQ 3: Strava's access tokens expire six hours after they are created and each refresh returns a new refresh token.
quote: Access tokens expire six hours after they are created, so they must be refreshed in order for an application to maintain access to a user

claim: Table / FAQ 3: Strava returns a new refresh token with every new access token.
quote: Every time you get a new access token, we return a new refresh token as well.

claim: On-device section: an app doesn't know whether read permission was granted or denied.
quote: As part of the privacy protections, your app doesn’t know whether someone granted or denied permission to read data from HealthKit.

claim: On-device section: people can change your app's permissions at any time in Settings or Health.
quote: A person can change the permissions for your app at any time using either the Settings or Health app.

claim: On-device section: people can grant only a limited window of recent data.
quote: In addition, people can choose to grant your app access to only a limited window of recent data rather than their full history.

claim: On-device section: users grant or deny permission separately per data type.
quote: Users can grant or deny permission separately for each type of data.

claim: On-device section: an app isn't aware when the user denies read permission; no data appears to exist.
quote: To prevent possible information leaks, an app isn’t aware when the user denies permission to read data. From the app’s point of view, no data of that type exists.

claim: On-device section: Health Connect requires per-app permission to read and write.
quote: Health Connect requires you to request the user's permission to read and write their health and fitness data on a per-app basis.

claim: On-device section: Health Connect uses the standard Android permission declaration format.
quote: Health Connect uses the standard Android permission declaration format.

claim: On-device section: one permission per data type, such as heart rate and steps.
quote: android.permission.health.READ_HEART_RATE

claim: On-device section: the Health Connect APK sits on the user's device.
